name: Mohanad Yehia
headline: Complex systems.
Clear evidence.
introduction: Production QA across web, mobile, API, and data.
bio: I'm a Software QA Engineer with production QA ownership at Blue Ribbon and enterprise testing experience through an Atos internship. My work connects test design, investigation, automation, and the evidence behind a release decision.

experience.summary: End-to-end QA for a production club-management platform spanning a Flutter mobile app, multi-tenant admin portal, REST API, PostgreSQL, payments, and ERP integration.
highlights: Tested cross-module journeys including wallet and payments, dining, bookings, academies, access control, and CRM notifications.
Led testing through the first production launch and legacy-system migration, using SQL verification to investigate backend issues and data integrity.
Built Selenium/Python automation, then migrated the admin-portal framework to Playwright/TypeScript with traces, video, and release-triggered CI.
Evaluated Appium before adopting Maestro for reusable mobile flows across authentication, wallet, dining, and booking journeys.

experience.summary: Training and project testing on MCIT's Personal Data Protection Centre platform, working with the senior QA team through the sprint cadence.
highlights: Authored 90+ test cases across 25 user stories covering roles, integration gates, document eligibility, fees, and payment paths.
Built a Bruno collection for Submit Inquiry covering four requestor types and seven negative or validation scenarios.
Reported an unhandled 500 exposing internal CRM names and error codes mapped to the wrong entity type.
Executed the Regularization suite against staging and logged defects in Azure DevOps.

experience.summary: Completed a 120-hour IT training programme involving Oracle Forms, ASP.NET MVC, networking, system administration, and internal documentation.
Prepared and executed 20+ SAP S/4HANA Sales and Distribution test cases across master data and transactional flows for 5+ departments.

approach.title: Find the risk
approach.description: Read the business flow, identify the costly failure, and make the assumptions explicit.
approach.evidence: Payments and cross-module journeys at Blue Ribbon; scheduling boundaries in Cal.diy.

approach.title: Follow the evidence
approach.description: Check the interface, API, and stored data against the same expected behavior.
approach.evidence: API contracts, booking lifecycle checks, SQL verification, and reproduced defect reports.

approach.title: Automate with intent
approach.description: Put repeatable checks at the useful layer and retain traces when something fails.
approach.evidence: Playwright, Maestro, API suites, and release-triggered CI.

approach.title: Keep the limits visible
approach.description: Separate a passing check from a justified quality decision.
approach.evidence: Unchanged accessibility failures, flake evidence, and a judge excluded from gates.
